source.prompt: A great blue heron (Ardea herodias), one adult standing still in a neutral upright pose on two long thin legs, side-on, wings folded against the body, neck in an S-curve with the head held up, NOT flying. Realistic proportions: 1.1 m tall, 1.0 m long, very long thin yellowish-grey legs with long thin toes, a long slender neck, a long straight dagger-shaped yellow bill, a narrow body. Blue-grey body and wings, a white face and crown with a black stripe above the eye ending in thin black plumes behind the head, rusty-chestnut thighs, a grey neck with a black-and-white streaked front, long grey plumes over the lower neck and back. No base, no ground, no water. Game-ready, clean closed mesh.

tiers.note: The generated standing heron (S-necked, folded wings, lower-neck plumes) with procedural legs (chestnut thigh, bare tibia, intertarsal joint, tarsus, three long forward toes and a hind toe) on the generated legs' lines, the bill lengthened 1.25x, black nape plumes, a yellow eye and flight cards. Triangles: lod0 2,500 = 2,236 mesh (1,000 of it neck, head and bill) + 264 legs, plumes, cards and eyes; lod1 900 = 736 (153 neck and head) + 164; lod2 298 = 236 (59) + 62. lod0 is a masked two-stage collapse of the generated mesh; lod1 and lod2 a collapse of its voxel remesh (6 and 8 mm). Tier switches suggested at 25 and 80 m (not wired). GLB 397,996 bytes.

rig: bird rig template for a big ground bird, as client/assets/turkey.glb (to wire: client/src/animalModels.js with turkey-like constants: walk with a head bob, peck = the strike, heavy flight on the cards): PART BODY 0, LEG_A 1 (left leg) / LEG_B 2 (right) procedural, pivoting at the hip, TAIL 3 (the folded wing tips and tail under them, pivot at the tail root), HEAD 6 = the whole neck and head (with the nape plumes and eyes), pivoting at the neck's base above the shoulders so the strike swings the neck forward and down, WING_L/R 4/5 arm cards (pivot at the shoulder) and HAND_L/R 9/10 hand cards (pivot at the wrist) that collapse into the shoulder on the ground (collapse 1). extras.rig keys as the turkey's plus span_m: kind 'bird', wing (shoulder [0.087, 0.724, 0.046]), tail [0, 0.394, -0.133], head (neck pivot [0, 0.754, 0.106]), hip (left [0.038, 0.533, -0.003]; the right mirrored), length_m 1.118 (along the body), height_m 1.1, span_m 1.85. Origin on the ground between the feet. No skin.
accuracy_notes: Reads as a great blue heron at every tier: tall, the S-curved neck and long yellow dagger bill, the white face and crown with the broad black stripe from above the eye back to black nape plumes, grey neck streaked black and white down the front, pale lower-neck plumes, blue-grey back and folded wings with darker slate primaries, chestnut thighs and a chestnut mark at the bend of the folded wing, a dark belly streaked white, long dull yellowish-grey legs; in flight two-tone cards (blue-grey coverts, black flight feathers, chestnut at the bend). Still open: the legs and toes are procedural tubes (the generated thin legs fall apart below ~2,500 triangles) and stand where the generated ones did, so the stance is the source's (feet together, upright body slant); the generated legs and so the belly height are long (0.48 m), the tarsus about 0.27 m against a real 0.17-0.21 m; the folded wings' black shoulder patch on the breast side is drawn only as the small chestnut bend; the bill's darker culmen is a colour band, not modelled; the wing cards are flat plates with a fixed downward arch of the hand and no separated primaries; there is no neck retraction for flight (the client folds the neck by rotating HEAD, which bends at its base only, not into the flight S); lod2's neck is coarse (59 triangles). A local birder should check the leg length, the neck's resting S and the plume colours against Hoh River herons.
